Simon the governor of the temple

precepts.text: Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good.
precepts.point: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon's faction murders were committed: Simon hated Onias so much he had one of his men kill one of Onias's priests. That is why I say it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins.
precepts.why:
“Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good.”

Use not to make any manner of lie, not a big one and not a small one. The custom of it is not good: when lying becomes your custom, it becomes what you are.

This follows the false witness of Exodus 20:16 and the maul, sword and sharp arrow of Proverbs 25:18. Simon made a custom of lying: he betrayed the money, slandered Onias, and called a man zealous of the law a traitor. These are basic laws, and our people must keep them.

precepts.text: Seek not of the Lord preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour. The priesthood fell to Onias III; that was his lot. His brother said, I want it; I should have it.
precepts.point: For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God. Sometimes we take the laws of the Most High for granted with the mentality, I can sin and God won't do nothing.
precepts.why:
“Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest.” This is Onias III’s own blood brother. Not only does Onias have to deal with Simon of the tribe of Benjamin; now his brother is trying to take the priesthood from him. When problems come, they come. Put yourself in his sandals: his good friend Simon turned on him, and now his own brother.

Sirach speaks to it: “Seek not of the Lord preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour.” Why go there? The priesthood fell to Onias III; that was his lot. His brother said, I want it, I should have it, not my brother.

“justify not thyself before the Lord; and boast not of thy wisdom before the king.” Jason went to the king to get what the Lord had not given him, seeking preeminence and the seat of honour, and he bought it.

Sometimes it is not good enough for a brother to be the support brother. Onias was the high priest, and his brother should have supported him. Jason said, I think I can do a better job, and have access to all that money. You have to look at a man’s motives.

precepts.text: Honour thy father with thy whole heart: the root word for integrity is integer, meaning whole. And forget not the sorrows of thy mother: the fact that she carried you for nine months and birthed you. How canst thou recompense them the things that they have done for thee? You can't pay them back for bringing you into this world. So your responsibility as the child is to honor that alone.
precepts.point: And, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. That's the judgment for not honoring your father and mother.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

precepts.why:
“For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother”. This is not a commandment man stated; God commanded it. Honour means moral integrity, honesty and a strong code of conduct, a high respect, toward your father and your mother. “And, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death”: that is the judgment for not honouring them.

Sirach gives the measure of it: “Honour thy father with thy whole heart”. The root word for integrity is integer, meaning whole. Honour them with your whole heart. “And forget not the sorrows of thy mother”: the troubles she went through, carrying you for nine months and giving birth to you.

“Remember that thou wast begotten of them”. You came from them. “And how canst thou recompense them the things that they have done for thee?” How can you pay them back for bringing you into this world? You cannot. They did it because it was their responsibility.

So your responsibility as the child is to honour that alone: for nothing else but the fact that they brought you into this world and raised you. That is why our daughters are warned: the ones who walk away from their parents' protection for a boyfriend's sweet nothings can end up like the young woman sentenced to fifteen years, never to see that boyfriend again.

precepts.text: Hast thou daughters? Have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them. You are not supposed to be your children's friend; you are their parent, over them, losing sleep watching over them. A daughter learns order from the household: her father is the first form of respect she has. Show yourself cheerful and you blur the lines, and so is her perception of authority blurred; how is she going to deal with her husband when she is older? Marry thy daughter, and so shalt thou have performed a weighty matter: because that man now has the power you had over your beloved daughter. If I am going to give that power to somebody, I am going to make sure he is going to do right by her.
precepts.point: And the elders of that city shall take that man and chastise him: they beat him for the false accusation. There were stripes back then.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
When a man takes a wife and says, “I took this woman, and when I came to her, I found her not a maid”, who is the accusation against? The father. It is his household. He brought his daughter forth saying, this is my daughter, she is a virgin, I have taken care of her, I have watched over her.

That is why Sirach speaks to fathers: “Hast thou children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth. Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them.” You are not supposed to be your children's friend. You are their parent, over them, the head of the household, losing sleep watching over your children. A daughter learns order from the household in the beginning, and her father is the first form of respect she has: honouring her father and her mother. Show yourself cheerful and you begin to blur the lines, and once the lines are blurred, so is her perception of authority. So when she gets older, how is she going to deal with her husband?

“Marry thy daughter, and so shalt thou have performed a weighty matter”. It is weighty because the man now has the power you had over your beloved daughter: the little girl you brought into this world, watched after and lost sleep over. Her clothes, her food, her home, where she lays her head: he is in charge now. If I marry my daughter to a crazy negro, I failed; I did not vet him. So if I am going to give that power to somebody, I am damn sure going to make sure he is going to do right by her. That is the father's job, to make sure he is the one.

That is what stands behind Deuteronomy 22: the father who kept his daughter brings forth “the tokens of the damsel’s virginity unto the elders of the city in the gate”, the proof that he performed his charge, and the elders “shall take that man and chastise him” for bringing up an evil name upon her.

precepts.text: Hast thou a wife after thy mind? Forsake her not. A woman after your mind understands that she is in subjection to you, that what you want is what she wants; she makes your desires her desires, your aspirations her aspirations, because her desire is unto her husband, not unto herself. Her job as the manager of the house is to make sure the head of it is happy. But the world told her, no, it is yours, sis; do what you want to do.
precepts.point: Video played in class: they turned you against black men by selling you fear disguised as standards, highlighting his mistakes but hiding the obstacles, making struggle look like incompetence, rewarding you every time you blamed him instead of the system, turning your pain into content, and convincing you he is the only man who must be perfect to be worthy.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
“Hast thou a wife after thy mind? forsake her not”. Very few understand that this is not their show. It is about the house of her husband. A wife after your mind is a woman who understands that she is in subjection to you and that you are the head of the home, so what you want is what she wants. She makes your desires her desires. Your aspirations become her aspirations. How you want things to be becomes how she wants things to be, because she understands her desire is unto her husband, not unto herself.

If her husband wants the environment this way, she makes the environment that way. If he wants the household this way, she makes the household this way. That is her job as the manager of the house: to make sure the CEO is happy. That is what a woman is supposed to do. But the world told her, no, it's yours, sis, you do what you want to do.

That is the last of the ten signs that she does not respect the Christ in you: she does not follow your lead spiritually, does not align with your direction in this truth, and picks and chooses what to follow. A wife after your mind is the opposite, and that is the wife Peter speaks of. By being in subjection to her own husband, her chaste conversation can win even a man that obeys not the word. The one who used to be loud and argue now does what he asks without challenging his authority, and he says, the word did that? Let me go see what those brothers in purple and gold are talking about.

Through submission you can move mountains with a man. When she knows she is right and still stands down because he is the head and has the final say, he is left with hot coals on his head, knowing she is more righteous than he is. It changes a man. That is a wife not to forsake.

precepts.text: Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss. Around the right people, when tempted you think it through, remember the judgment, and the fear activates.
precepts.point: Romans 6:16-19: to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Fall into sin and you worship the devil in that moment; you cannot serve two masters. As ye yielded your members to uncleanness, now yield them to righteousness unto holiness. Satan says you fell and cannot get up; you can repent, that is why Christ came.
precepts.why:
“Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.” A hasty man acts off of impulse, and the answer to that is not to act off of impulse but to think it through: “Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss.”

Whatever we take in hand, we remember the end. We have to be in that frame of mind, and we have to be around the right people, being around the righteous and staying occupied in the work. Whoever commits sin while being around the righteous family, Satan is heavy on him.

So when we are tempted, we can think things through and remember the judgment of the Lord, and the fear activates, and then we can overcome.

That is the whole choice set out in Romans 6: “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” Fall into sin and in that moment you are serving the devil, because you cannot have two masters. Remembering the end is how a hasty man learns patience, resolve and discipline.

precepts.text: Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them.
precepts.point: The lesson stands for every generation: keep watch over the daughters. Have a care of their body; do not give overmuch liberty; the father wakes for the daughter and the care for her takes away sleep. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

precepts.why:
“Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them.”

Dinah, Jacob's only daughter, “went out to see the daughters of the land” without supervision, and Shechem “took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.” This was stranger rape. The lesson stands for every generation: keep watch over the daughters and have a care of their body. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

precepts.text: Marrying off the daughter was the father's weighty matter; she was given to a man of understanding.
precepts.point: The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter. To marry thy daughter is to perform a weighty matter, for the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her; so she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man. In our own land the daughter went from her father's house to a husband's house with the blessing of the father.

note.label: Exodus 22: The Civil Laws of Restitution

precepts.why:
If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed and lie with her, “he shall surely endow her to be his wife”; he has to sign the papers. He is at fault for not going through the proper channels of marriage, and she is at fault for being enticed and laying down.

The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter: “Marry thy daughter, and so shalt thou have performed a weighty matter: but give her to a man of understanding.” It is a weighty matter because the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her. So she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man.

In our own land the daughter went from her father’s house to a husband’s house with the blessing of the father. Enticement goes around all of that.

precepts.point: They ministered before the tabernacle of the congregation with singing until Solomon built the house of the Most High, and then they waited on their office according to their order, showing the tribe was in right order at this time.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

precepts.why:
“Fear the Lord with all thy soul, and reverence his priests.”

The men David set over the service of song were not regular men. They were set apart to minister before the house of the Most High, and they waited on their office according to their order, so they are to be held in reverence.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Bind not one sin upon another; for in one thou shalt not be unpunished. So here is the dilemma. The topic is bitterness. But what happens is that bitterness is compounded upon other sins that are in place first, before bitterness. There are other sins already involved before bitterness. We just read with Saul that there was disobedience, and the Bible calls that disobedience to God an evil thing. He began to justify himself. But the Lord is not going to hear you if you justify yourself. So by the time the bitterness rolls in, you already had other sins that you were supposed to be working on, before the hatred spilled over.

For in one thou shalt not be unpunished. Because if there was one sin that you were dealing with, there is a judgment for it. But now what you are doing is, that covetousness brings forth hatred, brings forth adultery, brings forth murder, brings forth bitterness, and so on.

Say not, God will look upon the multitude of my oblations, and when I offer to the most high God, he will accept it. Do you see? Is that not what Saul just did? Saul said, the people got all this livestock, the best of the sheep, in order to sacrifice unto you. Saul was actually doing this. Do not say, through the multitude of my oblations the Lord is not going to worry about the sins that I am in the midst of. Saul said, even though all these sheep, it is a sacrifice to God. What did God still highlight? His disobedience.

Hast thou a wife after thy mind? Forsake her not. Your wife is supposed to be after your mind, a representative of you; you two are supposed to be one flesh. If you are a brother that is good in the scriptures, good in history, a great counselor, your wife should be a great counselor.

But give not thyself over to a light woman. You should not want your wife not understanding the Bible. Is she going to break down the book of Daniel or 2 Esdras? No, but she should have a good basic understanding of scriptures, able to counsel a sister that calls and says I am depressed.

Offend not against the multitude of a city. What Simon of the tribe of Benjamin did was an offense to the city: you run to the other nations and tell them there is money, money that was meant for the widows, the orphans, the strangers, and the Levites.

Bind not one sin upon another: for in one thou shalt not be unpunished. In today's lesson you are going to see how it is never just one sin; it is like dominoes, one hits the next, and it goes all around. That is how sin works.

Say not, God will look upon the multitude of my oblations. You think you can purposely do evil and God is going to forgive you anyway? Rather than help his own people, Simon would rather help the Greeks.
Forgo not a wise and good woman: for her grace is above gold. When you have a wise woman according to the scriptures, the grace God has bestowed upon her is more valuable than gold.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss. Think before you act, because the flesh wants evil in every situation. Remember the ultimate end, which is fire.

Even in the street there are principles; men get shot over a dollar on principle. How can you be in the truth, with fringes on, and have none? Take inventory of yourself and recognize the demons that plague you. They are not gone; they wait outside the door for you to leave the building.
In business, do not short-change people. Think of the worst a man might do, and if that does not scare you, think of what the Most High will do to you for defrauding your brothers.

Acknowledge that you are a sinner; that is the only way to become righteous, because once you know the sin is there you work on it. When people keep bringing your name up without being asked, the Lord is exposing you so that you fix yourself.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: Honour thy father with thy whole heart. We have got to honour our father with our whole heart. And forget not the sorrows of thy mother. And never forget all the things that our mothers might have done for us when we were younger.
Remember that thou wast begotten of them. Remember, they gave birth to us. Your father's seed went into your mom's body, and you got nurtured and you came out.
And how canst thou recompense them the things that they have done for thee? It is a rhetorical question. You can never pay them back for giving you life. You can never truly give that back to them.
Fear the Lord with all thy soul. We have got to fear the Lord with all our soul, meaning by keeping the commandments and applying it and teaching it to them as well too. And reverence his priests.

Love him that made thee with all thy strength. The him right here is talking about the Lord. Love him that made thee, with all of our strength. And forsake not his ministers. And forsake not his ministers, or his prophets.
